A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (Study Effisayil-1) [NCT03782792] was conducted to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of SPEVIGO in adult subjects with flares of generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP).

The Applicant conducted a randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2 trial (1368-0013) to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and tolerability of a single 900 mg intravenous dose of spesolimab (BI 655130) compared with placebo in subjects with GPP presenting with an acute flare.

design.text: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to a single 900 mg intravenous dose of spesolimab or placebo on Day 1

citations.quote: The Applicant conducted a randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2 trial (1368-0013) to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and tolerability of a single 900 mg intravenous dose of spesolimab (BI 655130) compared with placebo in subjects with GPP presenting with an acute flare.

The trial was designed to randomize 51 treatment-eligible subjects (i.e., subjects experiencing an acute GPP flare as defined above) in a 2:1 ratio to receive a single dose of 900 mg of spesolimab or placebo on Day 1 (Visit 2).

population.text: Adults with GPP flare of moderate-to-severe intensity (GPPPGA total score of at least 3), presence of fresh pustules, GPPPGA pustulation subscore of at least 2, and at least 5% body surface area covered with erythema and pustules

citations.quote: Substantial efficacy was demonstrated in one pivotal Trial 1368-0013, which enrolled 53 adult subjects with GPP flare of moderate-to-severe intensity defined as a Generalized Pustular Psoriasis Physician Global Assessment (GPPPGA) total score of at least 3 (moderate) [the total GPPPGA score ranges from 0 (clear) to 4 (severe)], the presence of fresh pustules (new appearance or worsening of pustules), GPPPGA pustulation sub score of at least 2 (mild), and at least 5% body surface area covered with erythema and the presence of pustules.

endpoint.text: Proportion of subjects with a GPPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 (indicating no visible pustules) at Week 1 after treatment

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) are asthenia and fatigue (9%), nausea and vomiting (9%), headache (9%), pruritus and prurigo (6%), infusion site hematoma and bruising (6%), and urinary tract infection (6%). Infections occurred in 14% of SPEVIGO subjects vs 6% placebo through Week 1. Serious hypersensitivity reactions including DRESS were reported in two subjects exposed to spesolimab in trial 1368-0013.
